items: Egypt's annual headline inflation eases to 12% in October from 12.8% in September, with monthly inflation at 0.6% → slower inflation after the CBE's 100 bp hike widens the real rate and supports the case for holding rates.
Goldman Sachs says the pound is more than 30% undervalued and sees it at 50 per dollar in 12 months → a top bank's buy call can draw carry-trade money back into Egyptian debt.
The cabinet raises export rebates by an average of 35% and covers up to half of freight costs to new markets → the EGP 48 bn programme aims to lift exports and bring in more dollars.

The US sets up a task force to cut Iran's land supply routes as more blasts hit Qeshm and two tankers strike mines near Hormuz → the war widens even as Qatar-mediated talks continue, keeping oil and shipping risk high.

Cabinet orders three months of spending cuts: government electricity use down 20%, vehicle fuel down at least 30%, and no new projects or car purchases → the state is cutting its own fuel and dollar needs, a sign of fiscal strain but also of lower demand for FX.

The pound ends the week at EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE, with the dollar down about 2.12 pounds (3.78%) over the week → foreign money returns to Egyptian T-bills, and one banker sees 50 to 52 if inflows last.
Brent ends Friday at $98.32 as oil futures post their biggest weekly drop since 2022 → Gulf exports recover and traders bet on a faster end to the Iran war, which eases Egypt's import bill.
EGX30 ends the week at 51,152.73, up about 4.9% from Sunday's close (derived) after three straight gains → the pound's rally and falling oil bring buyers back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

EGX30 rises 0.99% to 51,152.73 on Thursday, its third straight gain, with 169 stocks up and foreigners the only net buyers → a firmer pound and lower oil bring foreign money back; market cap reaches EGP 4.05 tn.

The pound strengthens to EGP 54.01 per dollar at the CBE on Thursday evening, after 54.77 on Wednesday → foreign investors turn net buyers of Egyptian T-bills ($112.3 mn on Wednesday) as oil falls, easing dollar demand.
Net international reserves reach a record $57.5 bn at end-October, up about $152 mn from September → a record buffer gives the CBE more room to support the pound as the IMF programme nears its end.

Brent rebounds 3.9% to $98.29 on Thursday after tanker attacks in Hormuz, a day after an 8.7% fall → Iran says Hormuz stays shut until its seven conditions are met, so oil swings remain a risk to Egypt's import bill.

Brent settles 8.7% lower at $94.62 on Wednesday, its first close under $100 since September, after Vance blames the midterm defeat on the Iran war → markets bet Washington wants out of the war; oil down more than 14% this week sharply cuts Egypt's fuel and LNG import bill.
The pound gains 65 piasters in one session to EGP 54.77 per dollar at the CBE → falling oil and the 100 bp hike ease dollar demand; a stronger pound lowers import costs and inflation pressure.

EGX30 jumps 2.83% to 50,650.18, back above 50,000, as 197 stocks rise and foreign institutions net buy EGP 338.7 mn → peace hopes, cheaper oil and a firmer pound pull foreign money back; pharma and consumer names lead.

Iran calls the US reply to its Hormuz plan unconvincing but Qatar says both sides stay committed, and Trump tells the FT he has no immediate plans to strike → talks continue despite attacks on shipping, keeping a deal and lower energy costs in play for Egypt.
The EBRD, the IFC and Helikon each disclose about 6.9% of Banque du Caire after buying EGP 16.7 bn of shares at EGP 5.30 → anchor foreign holders give the new listing a stable shareholder base.

Democrats win both chambers of Congress in the US midterms, with CNBC projecting at least 245 House seats and at least 51 in the Senate → a divided Washington constrains Trump's agenda for the rest of his term, including war spending, as talks with Iran continue.

EGX30 rebounds 1.76% to 49,255.66 on Tuesday, ending a four-session fall, as 180 stocks rise and foreigners net buy about EGP 130 mn → a firmer pound and lower oil bring back foreign buyers; developers and Eastern Company lead while fertiliser names fall.

Gas supplies to fertilizer plants are cut 20% while Egyptian urea sells at $535 a ton, about 17% above September → LNG cargoes now cost over $100 mn each, so the state rations gas; Abu Qir confirms the cut and falls 3.59%.

Brent settles 1% lower at $103.60, its lowest close since 7 October, as traders weigh US-Iran talks → Iran calls the US reply unconvincing, but Qatar expects both sides' feedback within 36 hours; lower oil eases Egypt's import bill.

The government weighs selling a large EgyptAlum stake on the EGX before year-end, after Banque du Caire raised $658 mn → the state targets $1.5 bn of offerings this year; a new listing would add depth for brokers and investors.

key.l: gas cut to fertiliser and methanol plants, up from 20%

stories.h: Government deepens gas cuts to 33% for fertiliser plants and turns to steel
stories.what: Gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants rise to 33% from the 20% imposed on 1 November; MOPCO confirms the new level in a bourse filing, while Abu Qir and Kima confirm only 20%. Ezz Steel is told of a 30% cut from 8 November, Asharq Business reports, though Ezz has not confirmed it. The JKM LNG benchmark rises about 36% in October to over $34 per mmBtu, and the government defers five of 15 cargoes contracted for November. Neither cut has an end date.
stories.why: Costlier LNG makes imports expensive, so the state keeps gas for power plants; one spot cargo costs close to $120 mn, an official says.
stories.aff: Urea exports (about 3.6 mn tonnes of spare capacity a year), steel output and Egypt's export earnings.
stories.eg: Fertiliser exports earned $2.53 bn in the first nine months of 2026; lower output cuts that just as urea sells at about $535 a tonne.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertiliser and steel makers; the cost of the cuts is not yet quantified.
stories.names: MOPCO, Abu Qir Fertilizers, Kima, Ezz Steel (bearish).

stories.h: EGX30 slips 0.67% as fertiliser stocks drop nearly 6%
stories.src: Amwal Al Ghad; Arab Finance; StockAnalysis.com
stories.what: The EGX30 falls 0.67% to 50,812.07 on Sunday after three days of gains, while the EGX70 rises 0.68% and the EGX100 0.28%. Turnover is EGP 10.52 bn and market cap ends at EGP 4.04 tn. Foreigners net sell EGP 27.9 mn while Egyptians and Arabs net buy. MOPCO falls 5.85% and Abu Qir Fertilizers 5.78%, while Edita gains 3.67% and Elsewedy 1.54%.
stories.why: Deeper gas cuts hit fertiliser makers; the wider market takes a breather after last week's rally.
stories.aff: Fertiliser stocks, blue chips and small caps.
stories.eg: Small caps keep rising while large caps pause.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertilisers; mixed for the rest of the market.
stories.names: MOPCO, Abu Qir Fertilizers, Credit Agricole Egypt (down); Edita, Elsewedy, Telecom Egypt (up).

key.l: Brent in Asian trade, Mon 9 Nov, -1.5%

stories.h: US land blockade on Iran takes effect as Trump plays down new strikes
stories.what: Trump says the US blockade of Iran's land supply routes is in effect, and Tehran threatens a harsh response if attacks resume. Trump says renewed strikes are very unlikely if talks on the nuclear programme and Hormuz progress, and plans to discuss Iran with Xi and Putin at APEC. A drone attack halts output at Iraq's Khor Mor gas field. Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 and WTI 1% to $89.85 in Asian trade.
stories.why: Markets price "a relatively optimistic scenario of de-escalation", one analyst tells Reuters.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf shipping and regional gas supply.
stories.eg: Lower oil eases Egypt's fuel bill, but Gulf gas disruption keeps LNG costly.
stories.egx: Neutral; oil relief is offset by gas tightness.

key.l: Evergreen's absence from the Suez Canal before Sunday

stories.h: Evergreen returns to the Suez Canal after nearly three years
stories.what: The 16,556-container Ever Eon crosses the canal on Sunday on the Ocean Alliance's NEU 7 service from the Netherlands to Singapore. SCA chairman Osama Rabie says Evergreen plans more transits and that CMA CGM, Maersk, MSC, Hapag-Lloyd and COSCO have also returned to the Europe-Asia route.
stories.why: Carriers that left during the Red Sea crisis are routing through Suez again.
stories.aff: Canal fees, port services and Egypt's dollar income.
stories.eg: Higher canal traffic adds dollar revenue and supports the pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for shipping, port and logistics names.

key.l: new Orascom Construction shares for the OCI merger

stories.h: Orascom Construction approves 97.2 mn new shares for its OCI merger, listing on 24 November
stories.what: Orascom Construction's board approves issuing 97.2 mn new shares to OCI, raising issued capital to $207.4 mn from $110.2 mn. The shares list on the EGX and ADX on 24 November, OCI leaves Euronext Amsterdam on 27 November, and completion is expected in December ahead of a 30 December long-stop date. The deal still depends on NNS's tender offer, which closes on 17 November.
stories.why: The merger combines two Nassef Sawiris-backed firms into one Abu Dhabi-based platform.
stories.aff: Orascom Construction's share count, free float and index weight.
stories.eg: A larger listed group could draw more foreign investors to the EGX.
stories.egx: Neutral to mildly bullish for Orascom; watch dilution and index changes.

stories.h: Drugmakers reportedly seek 20% price rises in the first test of the new pricing formula
stories.what: The EDA's formula, in force since 24 September, weights the exchange rate 60%, urban inflation 30% and the CBE deposit rate 10%, and needs a change of at least 10% held for 45 days. Drugmakers reportedly want 20%; the EDA says it has received no exceptional requests. CI Capital estimates the formula supports about 10% at EGP 56 per dollar, and says a recovery to 50 or 51 would likely rule out a rise.
stories.why: The weaker pound and costlier raw materials squeeze margins.
stories.aff: Drug prices, pharma margins and inflation.
stories.eg: Any rise reaches pharmacies only in late 2Q or 2H 2027, CI Capital says.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for listed drugmakers if the pound stays weak.

stories.h: Egypt draws 16.2 mn tourists by October and targets 20 mn this year
stories.what: Tourism Minister Sherif Fathy says Egypt hosts about 16.2 mn tourists by the end of October and targets 20 mn by year-end and 22 mn in 2027. Tourism revenue reaches $18.4 bn in FY2025/26, up 10.3%, according to CBE data. Fathy says Egypt needs more hotel rooms and airport capacity.
stories.why: Arrivals hold up despite the regional war.
stories.eg: Tourism is one of Egypt's largest sources of dollars.
stories.egx: Bullish for tourism and hospitality names.
